steps.speaker: Gentle Female Voice
steps.content: Youyou, have you memorized the new passage from yesterday?

steps.speaker: Youyou?
steps.content: Yes, yes! I know it! Fortune and misfortune come not unbidden, but through our own doing. The fruit of good and evil follows us, just like... like one's shadow!

steps.speaker: Gentle Female Voice
steps.content: Excellent! Now, do you understand what those words mean?

steps.speaker: Youyou?
steps.content: A senior disciple explained it to me! It means our actions determine our fortune, so good deeds bring good fortune, and bad deeds bring misfortune!

steps.speaker: Kind Male Voice
steps.content: Your mother and I have chosen a nickname for you—Wuhuanzi. When you grow up, if you also wish to...

steps.speaker: Gentle Female Voice
steps.content: Oh my, it's too early for such talk. All we wish is for Youyou to grow up healthy and carefree.

steps.speaker: Gentle Female Voice
steps.content: Whether she wants to inherit this nickname or become a healer, it's all up to her.

steps.speaker: Kind Male Voice
steps.content: Youyou, here's another saying I want you to know: A single act of kindness can ward off a hundred calamities.

steps.speaker: Kind Male Voice
steps.content: Whenever you feel chased by bad luck, just remember to be kind. The good karma you accumulate will help ward off all your troubles.

steps.speaker: Youyou?
steps.content: Like how you heal people and save lives?

steps.speaker: Gentle Female Voice
steps.content: Ah yes, that's right. The more good we do, the better this world becomes.

steps.speaker: Panicked Male Voice
steps.content: The disaster is here! Run!

steps.speaker: Kind Male Voice
steps.content: Someone's injured here! Quick! Stop the bleeding!

steps.speaker: Gentle Female Voice
steps.content: Tie a tourniquet around the severed limb. Needle the vital points, then...

steps.speaker: Kind Male Voice
steps.content: Watch out! Rockfall! Ugh...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: No... Father! Mother! Someone help us!

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: M... Monsters?! People are turning into monsters?!

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: N-no, stay back!

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: How could this happen... The Vale is gone...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...Didn't you say healing others would save the world? Father, Mother, you lied to me...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Didn't you tell me doing good deeds could ward off all troubles? Then why... why did you leave me...

steps.speaker: Senior Disciple A
steps.content: There's nothing wrong with healing others. But, this was a calamity that no one could have escaped.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Father, Mother... None of us did anything wrong. We healed people and saved lives. Why were we still struck by such a tragedy?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Please, I can't make sense of it... Was our faith not strong enough?

steps.speaker: Senior Disciple A
steps.content: Youyou, stay strong! It must... it must be that our spiritual cultivation was still lacking!

steps.speaker: Senior Disciple B
steps.content: Y-yes, that's right! We hadn't earned enough good karma to ward off such a destructive disaster!

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: So... so that's why?

steps.speaker: Senior Disciple B
steps.content: That must be it! There can be no other reason...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: That disaster destroyed the Healer Vale and took my parents from me.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I survived narrowly and even awakened my special power. But with it came this misfortune that has haunted me ever since.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: My fellow disciples were like family to me. They comforted me and encouraged me to overcome my grief.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I had no time to dwell on my sorrow. With Eastia ravaged by disasters and sickness, I set out on my journey to heal and save as many as I could.
Wuhuanzi speaks softly, her gaze traveling across the winding streets of the Drifter Camp and lingering on the half-rebuilt structures at its edges.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Throughout my journey, I've saved many lives... and lost just as many.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I once thought I could wrestle lives from death's grasp, but in the end, I realized how powerless I truly was... When the world itself is crumbling, what can one person do to stop it?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: All my medical knowledge means nothing in the face of the calamity.
She lets out a long, heavy sigh, each word of this painful truth seeming to drag itself unwillingly from her lips.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I watched helplessly as those I had healed were slaughtered by monsters, crushed by falling rocks, burned alive in flames. The dying transformed into monsters themselves, while the survivors lost their homes and families...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I've convinced myself that I'm only healing others to earn good karma, as instructed by the ancient texts, and attribute my misfortune to not having done enough.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: But every time I try to save someone, I'm terrified.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Is the act of saving lives ultimately meaningless? Am I truly saving them, or merely changing the way they'll meet their end?
Wuhuanzi's voice catches in her throat as she looks up at you, tears welling in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Have I been wrong all along? In a world like this... it's pointless to try to save someone's life, isn't it?
Like someone drowning, she's desperately grasping for anything that might keep her afloat.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You choose to save others because that's who you are, someone with a kind heart.
Children dash past with playful shouts. Street vendors call out their wares. Warm light spills from the windows of homes, carrying the sound of laughter.
It all feels so ordinary, so beautiful, as if things like Mania, Corruptors, and Black Rings all only belong in some distant world.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Look around you. These simple moments of daily life continue because of the lives you've saved. Isn't that the point?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You've come such a long way on your own, witnessed so much death and despair, yet you've never stopped trying to save lives. That takes remarkable strength.
Following your gaze, Wuhuanzi looks out at the Drifter Camp. She's seen these daily scenes countless times before, but always through the eyes of a doctor searching for patients.
All she saw was people's illnesses and all she cared about was rushing to cure them, never realizing that saving lives meant more than the simple matter of life and death.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The difficult task of saving lives took its toll on you, so you found yourself an excuse... or rather, an anchor to hold onto.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It does help steady your heart and numb the pain. But like any anesthetic, its effects grow weaker over time...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm glad you shared this with me. It means you're starting to trust me, aren't you?
Wuhuanzi nods, sniffling slightly as she collects herself.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You asked me earlier, if I knew that saving someone now might expose them to greater dangers later, and I might be misunderstood by others for it, would I still offer my help.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Of course I would.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Those people who just came to share their stories and express their gratitude, they're the ones I've saved. I could never stand by and watch them die.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: There's only so much I can do, and those I've saved still face many challenges ahead. Some of them are doing well now, while others are worse off than before.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Do they ever regret being saved by you?
You smile.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Hmm... I don't know, but I do know that the dead have no chance for regret.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Before saving someone, do you ever consider what might happen to them afterward?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I mean, is there really time for that?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Choosing not to save someone leads to only one outcome—death. But choosing to save them creates endless possibilities, both for them and for yourself.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Even if death will still claim them in the end?

steps.speaker: Option
options: Even if death will still claim them in the end.

choices.text: Even if death will still claim them in the end.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The existence of something cannot be undone.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: People may die, but the memories we share with them live on. Buildings may crumble, but as long as their builders survive, they can be rebuilt.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Take this area and West District. Some places have been reduced to ruins, while others have risen again with towering new buildings. Even ruins themselves become historic landmarks that people remember and visit.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've saved others, and others have saved me in turn. That's the sole reason I'm still standing here with you today.
As Wuhuanzi listens intently, understanding seems to be dawning on her.
You reach the memorial at the foot of the Drifter Camp. Though reconstruction here isn't complete yet, some camp residents are voluntarily clearing away the scattered rubble.
You and Wuhuanzi keep your distance, not wanting to disturb their work.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Death is never meaningless. Things happen, and people remember.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This memorial stands for all those who gave their lives for the Drifter Camp and the mine.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No matter how many times this place is destroyed, people will rebuild it again and again. It's because of people like this that humanity's history continues to be written.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And to be honest, I don't really care about being remembered. I don't do what I do to leave behind a legacy, or achieve what people would call a happy ending.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Then why... What do you save lives for?
Realizing the conversation has gotten rather heavy, you shrug and stretch your stiff muscles.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Simply because I want to.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: That's it?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's it.
Wuhuanzi stares at you blankly, waiting for you to elaborate.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Well... I just couldn't stand by and do nothing, so I helped them out.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I... I don't understand. Saving lives is a complex task. Can the motivation really be that simple? A person's life or death affects so many people, so many things...
Seeing Wuhuanzi caught in another loop, you let out a resigned sigh, pondering how to help her break free from this mental maze.
Just then, a group of young people appears near you, the faint scent of incense still clinging to their clothes.

steps.speaker: Youngster A
steps.content: Let's hurry and clear this area. Ms. Wu was really concerned about rebuilding the memorial before she passed away.

steps.speaker: Youngster B
steps.content: Ms. Wu cared about so many things. Kids' education at the Drifter Camp, support for the elderly left on their own... We must carry on all these missions she left behind.

steps.speaker: Youngster A
steps.content: Of course we will! Ms. Wu sure kept herself busy after recovering from her leg injury, taking on so many responsibilities...
The young people chat casually as they work, white origami flowers pinned to their chests as they roll up their sleeves to clear away the rubble at their feet.
You gently nudge Wuhuanzi with your arm, gesturing for her to observe them.

steps.speaker: Youngster B
steps.content: But at least Ms. Wu was happy. She kept talking about that gifted young healer who cured her leg, saying she wanted to properly thank her if they ever met again...

steps.speaker: Youngster B
steps.content: Sigh, it's too late for that now... I wonder if that young healer came to Ms. Wu's funeral today...
Upon hearing them mention Ms. Wu and young healer, Wuhuanzi turns to you with disbelief in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Are they... Granny Wu's students?
You nod. Judging from their clothes and conversation, there's no doubt about it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You see? Even though Ms. Wu has passed away, treating her sure isn't meaningless, is it?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As you guys like to say in Eastia, every encounter happens for a reason. There must be a reason why we met them here today.
Wuhuanzi blinks.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: My friend, you're growing more and more knowledgeable about Eastian culture.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Actually... Before coming here, I was wondering if treating her legs somehow led to her accident.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: If I hadn't cured her self-righteously, she could still be reading by the window or making crochet dolls. She might not have ventured into danger and died such a meaningless death.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I couldn't accept Ms. Wu's eventual death despite my treatment. It's my one-sided regret. Am I forcing my will upon the natural order by thinking like this?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Perhaps your belief that she died a meaningless death is just as one-sided?
Your words seem to catch at a loose thread of Wuhuanzi's thoughts, gently beginning to unravel it. Under your gentle gaze, she reaches out and grasps it herself.
Wuhuanzi clenches her fists briefly, as if cheering for herself, then walks toward one of the youngsters.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Is Granny Wu's funeral... over?
When you return to the funeral, the mourners have already dispersed, leaving only Granny Wu's family to tend to the final arrangements.
The Drifter Camp is home to people from all walks of life, and their funerals are simple affairs, lacking the elaborate ceremonies common in Eastia.
Before you can get closer, a woman who has been watching anxiously by the door hurries over and takes Wuhuanzi's hands in hers.

steps.speaker: Emotional Woman
steps.content: Young healer, you came back! Thank goodness.

steps.speaker: Emotional Woman
steps.content: My brother and I were completely overwhelmed with the funeral arrangements. We only heard from the neighbors afterward that you'd come by, but got scared off by the crowd.

steps.speaker: Emotional Woman
steps.content: My brother went out looking for you while I waited here. And here you are!
The woman seems overwhelmed by sentiment. Unused to handling this kind of emotional display in others, Wuhuanzi turns to you with a helpless look.
Curious to see how she'll handle this, you pretend not to notice her discomfort and simply give her an encouraging look.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...Please accept my deepest condolences.
Wracking her brain, Wuhuanzi falls back on the most common Eastian condolence phrase she can think of.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: My mother spoke of you a lot. She would tell us how much you helped her when you were here, and what a dear, kind person you were.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: She was always worried about you, if you had a place to stay, if you were eating properly, or if law enforcement was bothering you.
Hearing about the old woman's constant concern for her, Wuhuanzi's throat tightens and she seems unable to hide her grievances any longer.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Your mother... she was truly a kind soul. She was the one who took me in when I couldn't afford to stay in an inn.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: When everyone else doubted me and refused my treatment, she gave me a chance, saying she hadn't been able to walk for years anyway.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Is there... anything I could do to help? Something I could do... for your mother?
Wuhuanzi asks gingerly.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: You've already done so much for us. My brother and I will take care of the funeral arrangements. Please don't worry.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: In fact, I wonder if we could do anything for you?
The woman looks at Wuhuanzi with such tender concern that it catches her off guard. The same kind of look you gave her not too long ago.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: Oh, I hope I'm not being presumptuous. It's just that you look so sad and aggrieved...
Touched by her kindness, Wuhuanzi gently waves her hand as she replies.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: May I know... after she regained her ability to walk, was your mother happy?

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: Of course, she was over the moon. And it wasn't just her, my brother and I were overjoyed to see her that way as well.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: Because of her leg, she hadn't left the Drifter Camp for many years. While we were away working, she spent most of her time alone at home.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: Her spirits lifted considerably. She used to be a teacher, so she even found a part-time nanny job in Eastside. She wouldn't stop telling us how full of energy she felt. She was even saving money to buy gifts for her grandchildren.
Hearing about Granny Wu's new life, a faint smile touches Wuhuanzi's lips. All the dreams her patient once shared about life after recovery had come true.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Then... how did she pass away?
Hearing the question, sadness washes over the woman's face.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: A few days ago, a rogue Corruptor appeared in the outskirts of Eastside. My mother was on an outing with her employers and their child at the time.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: She died protecting the child from the Corruptor, but her sacrifice bought enough time before the sheriffs arrived.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: No way...
Wuhuanzi's voice trembles.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: If... if she had stayed in the Drifter Camp, maybe she wouldn't have...

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: No, please don't think like that. She never regretted leaving home, and she would never regret saving that child.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: Though her death broke our hearts, we feel proud of her. She dedicated her whole life to nurturing children, and she died protecting one she loved.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: My mother always preferred tranquility, so we kept her funeral simple and quiet. We wanted her to depart this world in peace and serenity.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Was she... at peace when she passed? Did she... suffer at all?
After much hesitation, Wuhuanzi finally gathers the courage to ask what has been weighing heaviest on her mind.

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: It happened quickly, which was a mercy...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I see... That's a relief...
Wuhuanzi rubs her eyes and manages a bitter smile, her voice catching as she speaks.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: May I go in?

steps.speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
steps.content: Of course you can. My mother would have been very happy to see you.
The room, which was bustling earlier in the morning, now lies in silence. Though modestly furnished, everything is kept in perfect order, a testament to how much she cherished life.
On the table in the center of the room sits a photograph of an elderly woman, her gentle smile reaching her eyes.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Granny Wu, I'm here...
Wuhuanzi takes a white flower from the long table by the door and gently places it before the elderly woman's photograph.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I'm at a place called the Bureau now. I have a room there, food on my table, and someone who patiently answers all my questions. I can continue healing people and doing good deeds...
Wuhuanzi's throat tightens as her voice begins to quiver despite her best efforts.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I'm doing well, so wherever you are now... please don't worry about me.

A breeze drifts through the window, stirring the flower petals. Wuhuanzi's vision blurs with tears, but she stubbornly fights back a sob, quickly wiping away the tears with her sleeve before they can fall.
After bidding farewell to Granny Wu's daughter, you both leave the alley behind.
Wuhuanzi fiddles with a crochet doll given to her by Granny Wu's daughter. After regaining her zest for life, Granny Wu had made many such dolls to help support her family.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, young healer, did you find the answers you were looking for?
Wuhuanzi stops in her tracks and nods, taking a small step closer to you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You see, things aren't always as simple as they seem.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: When danger strikes, the urge to save others comes naturally. It's the same for Granny Wu. She did that because she had a kind heart, and so do you.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Then...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So stop talking about the crumbling world and how everything's beyond saving. Leave all these troubles to those big shots.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Is that really okay? Isn't it foolish to keep trying when it seems pointless?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yeah, it is pretty foolish. But thanks to that very foolishness, we've both managed to save quite a few people, haven't we?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Saving DisCity might seem impossible, but we can always help the person right in front of us, whether through a kind deed or a gentle word of guidance. Who knows? Once we've helped everyone we can reach, we might just find we've saved the world in the process.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: After all, the world is made up of the people you see. Whatever you witness, whatever you feel, that becomes your world.
After a long silence, you finally hear Wuhuanzi whisper something to her crochet toy.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I understand now. Whether something is truly foolish or meaningful... we'll never know unless we give it a try.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: From now on, I'll help everyone I want to help, whether it earns me good karma or not.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: My friend, thank you for bringing me to the Drifter Camp, and for walking this long path with me...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm glad you've found the answer. Mental turmoil is terrible for one's well-being. You keep trying to heal me, but you should take care of yourself as well.
Wuhuanzi raises her head, a warm smile playing across her face as she asks you.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Then... can I start by helping you?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Not for any particular reason. I simply want to. Even... even if you don't want my help, I'm going to help you anyway. And of course, free of charge!
Seeing the new hope in Wuhuanzi's eyes, you find it impossible to refuse.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Of course you can. Why don't we start with you helping me resolve the Mania-related issues at the Drifter Camp?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Ah, for instance... How about sealing that breach the Corruptor made on the east side? Maybe with your talismans...
Several days later, MBCC Chief's Office
Looking at the steaming herbal decoction on your desk, then at Wuhuanzi's stern little face, you finally realize just how rash your earlier decision was.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Do I really have to drink this?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: You must.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Can I please skip this one?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: No.
Wuhuanzi's gaze remains resolute, completely unmoved by your desperate pleas.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sigh...
You squeeze your eyes shut and try to convince yourself: Just pretend it's a budget version of the Bureau's signature coffee!
